paper.title_en: Structure of the neutron-rich <math><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>126</mn></mrow></math> isotones: A shell model analysis
paper.abstract_en: Shell model calculations for the neutron-rich <math><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>126</mn><mmultiscripts><mi>Hg</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>206</mn></mmultiscripts><mtext>-</mtext><mmultiscripts><mi>Lu</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>197</mn></mmultiscripts></mrow><mo> </mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>Z</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>80</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>71</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow></math> isotones were performed with two different parametrizations. The one refined to explain the isomerism in <math><mmultiscripts><mi>Pt</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>204</mn></mmultiscripts></math> was found to be the only one able to reproduce the more recent data on <math><mmultiscripts><mi>Ir</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>203</mn></mmultiscripts></math> and, in general, to give a better reproduction of the nuclei in this region. For more exotic nuclei approaching the <math><mi>r</mi></math>-process path, this refined parametrization predicts the existence of isomeric states with spin-parities <math><msup><mn>5</mn><mo>−</mo></msup></math> and <math><msup><mn>10</mn><mo>+</mo></msup></math> in the even-mass isotones and <math><mrow><mn>19</mn><mo>/</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mo>+</mo></msup></mrow></math> in the odd-mass isotones. Also, it predicts ground-state spin-parities of <math><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo>/</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mo>+</mo></msup></mrow></math> for <math><mmultiscripts><mi>Re</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>201</mn></mmultiscripts></math> and <math><mrow><mn>11</mn><mo>/</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mo>−</mo></msup></mrow></math> for <math><mmultiscripts><mi>Ta</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>199</mn></mmultiscripts></math> and <math><mmultiscripts><mi>Lu</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>197</mn></mmultiscripts></math>, with low-energy long-lived isomers present. The remaining deficiencies of the interaction are related to the properties of the <math><mrow><mi>π</mi><msub><mi>d</mi><mrow><mn>5</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math> orbital and are influenced by octupole collectivity. The presented predictions provide guidance and can be tested in the near future at radioactive-beam facilities.
